entities.summary: The Eastern Ganga dynasty were a large medieval era dynasty that reigned from Kalinga from as early as the 5th century to the mid 20th century. They are known as "Eastern Gangas" to distinguish them from the Western Gangas who ruled over Karnataka. The territory ruled by the dynasty consisted of the whole of the modern-day Indian state of Odisha, as well as major parts of north Andhra Pradesh, parts of Chhattisgarh and some southern districts of West Bengal. Eastern Gangas ruled much of the modern region of Odisha in three different phases by the passage of time, known as Early Eastern Gangas (493–1077), Imperial Eastern Gangas (1077–1436) and Khemundi Gangas (1436–1947).

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Eastern Ganga dynasty played a significant role in shaping the medieval history of South Asia, ruling over much of modern-day Odisha and parts of Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and West Bengal. Their three phases of rule contributed to the cultural, economic, and political development of the region.
